title: "My iman is low"
hook: Hanzalah feared he'd become a hypocrite because his faith faded at home; the Prophet ﷺ said: an hour, and an hour

segments.voice: Yesterday: tasbih, subhanallah, the word the whole world is already saying. Your line was glory. Today, the days when even one word feels far away.

A man walks through Medina saying, to no one in particular: Hanzalah has become a hypocrite. He means himself. Abu Bakr stops him. What are you saying? Hanzalah explains. When he sits with the Prophet ﷺ, hearing about the Garden and the Fire, it's as if he can see them. Then he goes home, to his wife, his children, his fields, and much of it slips away. The feeling is gone, and it frightens him. Today: what the Prophet told him.
screen: `HANZALAH HAS BECOME A HYPOCRITE.` → `WITH THE PROPHET, AS IF HE COULD SEE.` → `AT HOME, IT FADES.`

segments.voice: Abu Bakr's answer is the first surprise. By Allah, he says, I feel the same. The two of them go to the Prophet together, and Hanzalah says it again. The Prophet hears him out, then says, in Sahih Muslim: by the One in whose hand my soul is, if you stayed always as you are with me, and in remembrance, the angels would shake your hands in your beds and on your roads. But, Hanzalah: sa'atan wa sa'atan. An hour, and an hour. He says it three times. Muslims today have a phrase for what Hanzalah felt: my iman is low. You met iman on day five, a faith the Qur'an speaks of as growing. What grows can dip. The hadith doesn't call the dip hypocrisy; it treats it as being human: hours of nearness, and hours of the kitchen, the children and the fields. A report in later collections, which scholars grade differently, says faith wears out in the heart the way a garment wears out, so ask Allah to renew it. The Qur'an says: “Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!” Not a grand gesture. A word. Subhanallah, once, in the car. Many people feel the dip most right after Ramadan, when the month's high fades. Said gently: a dry stretch is one thing. If the low is heavy and won't lift, if sleep or hope are slipping, or if you've had thoughts of not being here, that's more than iman, and it deserves real help: a doctor, a counselor, someone you trust. In the US, call or text 988, any hour; elsewhere, local emergency help.
screen: `BY ALLAH, I FEEL THE SAME.` · `AN HOUR, AND AN HOUR.` · `WHAT GROWS CAN DIP. A WORD BRINGS IT BACK.` · `IF IT WON'T LIFT: REAL HELP, 988.`

segments.voice: Let the breath slow; no high is required. If you pray, say one word of remembrance on each breath out, subhanallah or alhamdulillah, like leaving a small light on in an empty room; if you don't, notice one thing you're grateful for. If the words feel hollow, say them anyway, gently, and let that be today's hour.
Sa'atan wa sa'atan. An hour, and an hour: the Prophet's answer to Hanzalah, that faith has its hours of nearness and its ordinary hours. Today's word.
Your line: an hour, and an hour. A low hour isn't the end of the story. Day one hundred fifteen.

howItsDone: Muslims often speak of iman rising and falling; in a low stretch many keep up small remembrance, a little Qur'an and good company, and many imams now also encourage seeing a doctor or counselor when the low is heavy or won't lift.

original.note: Arabic: an hour and an hour; sa'ah is an hour, a stretch of time. the Prophet ﷺ said it to Hanzalah three times.

trapdoor: what you thought: low iman means your faith was never real.
what it means: sa'atan wa sa'atan — faith has hours of nearness and ordinary hours, and the dip is human.
what a scholar hears: Hanzalah's hadith in Sahih Muslim 2750 (nafaqa Hanzalah); the garment report (al-Hakim, al-Tabarani, graded differently); 13:28 on hearts at rest; faith that increases (48:4).

notes: Rewritten 2026-10-06 from the five-year map; confirm with the Keeper.

NEW lesson from the map's #4 change ('low iman', the community's own phrase for spiritual dryness, never named as a lesson before: REDDIT.md #5). It replaces 'Alhamdulillah, thirty-three' (tahmid). Alhamdulillah itself is taught on day 11 (and line 2 of al-Fatiha on day 12); the thirty-three after the prayer is still laid out on day 114 and in Fatimah's set on day 116. The 'fills the scale' hadith (Muslim 223) is no longer taught in year 1.

Crisis care: the teach includes a gentle line pointing to a doctor or counselor and 988 (US) / local emergency help, per the owner's rule and THREADS_AND_COMMENTS.md §5 ('the lowest point is very literal').

Sahih Muslim 2750 paraphrased: Hanzalah al-Usayyidi meets Abu Bakr; 'nafaqa Hanzalah'; both go to the Prophet; 'if you remained as you are with me and in dhikr, the angels would shake your hands on your beds and in your roads, but, O Hanzalah, an hour and an hour', said three times. Confirm wording and number.

The garment report ('faith wears out in the heart of one of you as a garment wears out, so ask Allah to renew faith in your hearts'): al-Hakim's Mustadrak and al-Tabarani; graded sahih/hasan by some, weaker by others; the script says 'scholars grade differently'. Confirm the references.
Pickthall 13:28 quoted from memory ('...Verily in the remembrance of Allah do hearts find rest!'); please check.
Day 127 (Eid al-Fitr) now points back here for the post-Ramadan dip.
